$comment: Canonical shape of Prosary's domain model, independent of any one platform's language. Field names here are the camelCase form; each platform's own idiom (Swift camelCase, Kotlin camelCase, C# PascalCase) maps 1:1. See ../ARCHITECTURE.md for the prose version and per-file source locations. Keep this file in sync whenever a field is added, removed, renamed, or its default changes on any platform — see README.md in this directory.

isDefault.description: The starred/primary favorite for its devotion. At most one per (kind, customDevotionId) at a time — see persistence.perDevotionDefaultScoping below.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 code, or the empty-string sentinel meaning "follow the app-level default language setting" (see AppSettings.defaultLanguageCode).

customDevotionId.description: The bundle id (e.g. "angelus") whose devotion.json defines this favorite's step sequence. Populated only when kind == custom, null/nil otherwise. See PrayerEngine.buildCustomDevotionSteps and ARCHITECTURE.md's "Content bundles" section.

variantId.description: Which of the bundle's variants (alternate step-sets, e.g. the Stations' traditional vs. scriptural forms) this favorite prays. Null/nil = the bundle's default: the variant claiming the resolved prayer language via defaultForLanguages when one does, else the first declared; only meaningful when kind == custom and the bundle declares variants.

dayIndex.description: Multi-day (days-type) devotions: the day this favorite prays next, 0-based; advances when a day's session finishes (clamped by the engine so a completed devotion re-prays its last day). Null/nil = day 1. Only meaningful when kind == custom and the bundle's devotion is days-type.

customOptions.description: This favorite's choices for the bundle's options.json options, keyed by option key — "true"/"false" for toggles, a case id for choices. Only overrides: an absent key means the option's declared default. Persisted as one JSON column on every platform (customOptionsJSON Data / customOptionsJson TEXT / CustomOptionsJson TEXT). Only meaningful when kind == custom.

PrayerKind.description: Discriminant for the type of a saved prayer session. Only the Rosary (deeply configurable, options/calendar-driven) and the Jesus Prayer (a repetition counter with no steps) warrant their own cases; every other devotion is "custom".
PrayerKind.note: "custom" is the single case covering every generic, bundle-driven devotion (Angelus, Stations of the Cross, Franciscan Crown, Seven Sorrows, Divine Mercy Chaplet, Trisagion, ...) — adding a new generic devotion needs no new PrayerKind case, only a new .prosaryprayer bundle with a devotion.json. The five retired per-devotion cases' raw values double as the matching bundle ids; iOS/Android remap legacy persisted rows to custom + that id permanently at read time (resolvedKind), while Windows persists the enum as its int (Rosary=0, JesusPrayer=2, Custom=7 — explicit, permanent values) and runs a one-time PRAGMA user_version-guarded SQL migration. Never renumber or reuse a retired Windows ordinal (1, 3-6).

RosaryOptions.description: Configuration specific to the Rosary. Lives inside a Prayer when kind == rosary. Remains the persisted shape (typed columns, bespoke editor) even though the Rosary builds from the rosary bundle's devotion.json — PrayerEngine.rosaryOptionValues maps it onto the bundle's options.json values (no data migration).

specificMysteryGroup.description: Used when mysterySelectionMode == specific or singleMystery.

specificMysteryOrder.description: 1-based index into MysteryCatalog.forGroup(specificMysteryGroup) (always 5 mysteries per group). Used only when mysterySelectionMode == singleMystery.

includeOpeningPrayers.description: The opening Our Father + 3 Hail Marys (for faith, hope, charity) + Glory Be.

includeFatimaPrayer.description: "O my Jesus...", recited after the Glory Be of each decade.

includeClosingIntentions.description: The customary intercessions immediately after the Marian antiphon, each answered with an Our Father, Hail Mary, and Glory Be: for the Pope's intentions and the needs of the Church and the nation; for the local ordinary and his intentions (the Latin Patriarch in the vicariate's Hebrew, the exarch in the Mission of St. Gamaliel's overlay); and for the holy souls in purgatory, closed by "May they rest in peace. Amen." From the Mission of St. Gamaliel's prayer book (2026-08); ten bundle-driven closing steps gated on the rosary bundle's closingIntentions option.

presenterMode.description: Collapses each decade's 10 Hail Marys and its Glory Be onto one combined step (title "Hail Mary & Glory Be", body = both prayers' text) instead of 10 individual Hail Mary steps + a separate Glory Be step. Announcement and Our Father steps are unaffected. The combined step still sets hailMaryIndexInDecade = 10 so the bead-track UI renders the traditional 10-bead decade (see ARCHITECTURE.md).

mysteryImageStyle.description: Which artwork set illustrates the mysteries during the session. Maps onto the rosary bundle's imageStyle choice option; the engine resolves it by setting RosaryStep.imageVariantKey = "eastern_" + the mystery's imageKey on every step that carries a Mystery, so Mystery.imageKey itself (identity + translation lookup) is never touched.

MysteryImageStyle.description: The Rosary's mystery artwork set. classic = the public-domain classical paintings (default); eastern = the eastern/illuminated-manuscript-style icon set (eastern_* imageKeys). Windows persists this enum as a raw integer ordinal, so new cases must only ever be appended.

cases.description: Follow the traditional weekday assignment (with liturgical-season overrides on Sundays).
Always pray a specific, user-chosen set regardless of the day.
Joyful, Sorrowful, and Glorious (no Luminous), prayed in one session.
All 20 mysteries in one session, chronological order: Joyful, Luminous, Sorrowful, Glorious.

Always pray exactly one specific mystery (one decade), chosen via specificMysteryGroup + specificMysteryOrder. Appended last on every platform: Windows persists this enum as a raw integer ordinal, so new cases must never be inserted mid-list.

EternalRestPlacement.description: Where (if at all) "Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord" is prayed for the faithful departed.

cases.description: After the Glory Be of every decade.
Once, near the end, before the closing prayers.

MarianAntiphonOption.description: Which closing Marian antiphon (if any) follows the Rosary.

cases.description: Pick the antiphon proper to the current liturgical season automatically.
The Church's oldest known Marian prayer; traditionally recited on its own, without a versicle/collect.

JesusPrayerOptions.description: Configuration specific to the Jesus Prayer. Lives inside a Prayer when kind == jesusPrayer.

JesusPrayerTarget.description: How many times the Jesus Prayer is prayed in a session.

cases.description: No target; the user ends the session explicitly.

JesusPrayerProgress.description: Live repetition counter during a Jesus Prayer session. Not persisted. Immutable on Android/Windows (copy/with-based updates); a mutable struct on iOS — a deliberate, known divergence, not a bug.

PrayerReminder.description: One saved daily reminder time. Not a recurrence rule by itself — see reminders.schedulingStrategy in screens.json's sibling ARCHITECTURE.md section for how each platform turns this into an actual repeating notification.

code.description: ISO 639-1, used as the key into the content layer's translation dictionaries.

RosaryStep.description: One prayer "bead" in a fully built session for any devotion — the output of PrayerEngine.buildSteps(for:). See ARCHITECTURE.md#engines.

subtitle.description: Decade context, e.g. "1st Mystery — The Annunciation".

acclamation.description: Optional versicle/response prayer shown above the body in the regular prayer typeface, even when the body itself is scripture (the Stations, Via Lucis).

isScripture.description: True only for the mystery-announcement step, whose body is a real quoted Bible verse.

decadeIndex.description: 0-based, counted globally across every mystery group in the session — never resets per group. What the bead track uses to tell decades apart.

imageOverrideKey.description: For steps not tied to a Mystery that still want a specific illustration — see mysteries.json's overrideImages.

imageVariantKey.description: Alternate-artwork override, set by the engine on steps that carry a Mystery when the favorite's mysteryImageStyle asks for a non-default set (e.g. "eastern_joyful_01_annunciation"). Display resolution prefers it over everything: imageVariantKey ?? mystery.imageKey ?? imageOverrideKey ?? cross_placeholder. A separate field (not a rewritten Mystery.imageKey) because the mystery's own key is its identity and its translation-lookup key.

CustomDevotionStep.description: One entry in a generic devotion's devotion.json — a step of the flat "steps" type, an opening/closing step of the "rosary" type, or (closing only) a kind-tagged special step. See ARCHITECTURE.md's "Content bundles" section.

title.description: Literal English display string (the app-wide convention for step titles). Mutually exclusive with titleKey.

titleKey.description: Content key for devotions whose step titles are themselves translated content (the Stations' station names).

subtitle.description: Literal display string, e.g. "1st Station", "For the tears of Our Lady".

subtitleKey.description: Like titleKey for the subtitle — for subtitles that are themselves translated content (the Rosary's opening Hail Marys "for Faith/Hope/Charity"). Mutually exclusive with the literal subtitle.

bodyKey.description: Resolved bundle-raw-first (requested language, then the bundle's Latin), then the shared PrayerTranslations chain, then the raw key — see ARCHITECTURE.md.

acclamationKey.description: Resolved like bodyKey; emitted as RosaryStep.acclamation — the versicle/response rendered above the body in the regular prayer typeface (a scripture body's typeface never swallows it).

repeat.description: Unrolls into n steps titled "Title (h of n)" — deliberately without bead fields, matching the hardcoded devotions' closing Hail Marys.

isScripture.description: The body is a quoted Bible passage, so it renders in the scripture typeface (same flag the Rosary's mystery announcements carry). Set on the scriptural Stations' fourteen station steps.

isScriptureByLanguage.description: Per-session-language override of isScripture — for bodies that are quoted scripture in some languages but composed prose in others (the traditional Stations: Liguori meditations in la/en, scripture meditations in ar/he/ru/tl).

if.description: Gates this entry on one of the bundle's options.json options: "key" (toggle on), "!key" (toggle off), or "key=caseId" (choice equals) — evaluated against the bundle defaults overlaid with Prayer.customOptions; the entry is dropped when it fails. The validator checks every expression references a declared option/case.

kind.description: "seasonalMarianAntiphon" (closing only): emitted by the engine's shared, calendar-dependent antiphon builder instead of bundle data (the Franciscan Crown, and an hours-type closing). "marianAntiphon" (closing only): option-selected antiphon (the Rosary) — optionKey names a choice option whose value picks the antiphon, with "seasonal" calendar-resolved and "none" dropping the step. "proper" (hours type only): not a step at all but a named hole in an office — see slot/default below.

slot.description: kind == "proper": the name of this hole in the office ("psalmody", "hymn", "reading", "collect"). Whichever of the bundle's propers matches today with the highest precedence supplies the steps that stand here. Validator-enforced: some proper must be able to fill it, or it must carry a default, so a slot can never silently vanish from an office.

default.description: kind == "proper": the steps to use on a day no proper matches — how an author says "unless the calendar says otherwise, this".

optionKey.description: For kind == "marianAntiphon": the choice option whose value names the antiphon to build.

CustomDevotionDefinition.description: Parsed devotion.json — the complete structural description of a generic devotion. Field validity per type is enforced at authoring time by Shared/tools/validate-devotion.py; decoders are deliberately lenient (all optionals) so engines can switch on type alone.

type.description: "steps": a flat, fixed list (Angelus, Stations, Via Lucis, Trisagion). "rosary": decade/bead-structured (the Rosary itself, Franciscan Crown, Seven Sorrows, Divine Mercy). "days": multi-day (novenas, the 33-day Montfort consecration), worked through by a counter. "hours": several offices a day whose contents the liturgical calendar chooses (the Liturgy of the Hours) — format and validator only as of 2026-08-06; no decoders, engines or bundles ship yet.

days.description: days type only: [{name, nameByLanguage?, period?, steps: [Entry]}] — one entry per day, with optional shared opening/closing prayed every day. A series' progress lives in a MultiDayRun keyed by devotion id (start date + which days were prayed), not on the favorite; Prayer.dayIndex still holds the day a favorite opens on.

eastertideSteps.description: steps type only: whole-sequence swap during Eastertide (the Angelus's Regina Caeli substitution).

variants.description: Named alternate forms of one devotion, mutually exclusive with the type's own top-level fields; the first variant is the default, resolved via Prayer.variantId. **steps type**: [{id, name, nameByLanguage?, steps, eastertideSteps?}] — the Stations' traditional vs. scriptural sets. **rosary type** (2026-08-07): [{id, name, nameByLanguage?, opening, decades, closing, hasClosingCross?}] — a chaplet's shorter and fuller recensions, which can differ in their opening prayers, their per-decade invocations and their close while praying the same mysteries. Every rosary-type bead-track invariant is checked per form, not per bundle: a second form with no opening Sign of the Cross would crash the bead track exactly as a single-form devotion would. Any variant may declare defaultForLanguages: ["he-x-gamliel", …] (2026-08-08) — exact prayer-language codes, rites included, whose sessions open in it when Prayer.variantId is null; exact match only (a rite is a deliberate choice; its base language keeps the ordinary default), no two variants may claim the same code, and an explicit variantId always wins. Tradition-named variant ids must be declared in the canonical order latin → byzantine → west syriac → armenian → alexandrian → east syriac (validator-enforced): first-declared is the default, so the default belongs to the earliest tradition the bundle ships — the Latin form when there is one, else the Byzantine, and so on down.

opening.description: rosary, days and hours types; for rosary it may instead live inside each variant. For rosary, entry 0 MUST be the Sign of the Cross (bead-track invariant); for days it is prayed before every day's own steps, and for hours before every office.

dayProgression.description: days type only: "series" (default — consecutive days worked through in order, so the app tracks a run, advances by calendar day and can remind you each day; a novena, triduum or 33-day consecration) or "free" (the days are a set to pick from, like a prayer for each day of the week, with no run to be behind on).

suggestedReminderTime.description: days type, series only: "HH:mm" the author suggests for the daily reminder. Advisory — the user's own reminder times always win.

suggestedStart.description: days type, series only: "MM-DD" the series traditionally begins on, repeating annually (a novena to the Immaculate Conception starts "11-29"). Lets a pinned devotion announce itself — "Starts 29 November" — before its first day arrives. Advisory: starting it any day always works.

suggestedNext.description: days type, series only: the id of a devotion to offer when the last day is prayed — a novena ending on its feast can point at the feast-day prayer. May name a devotion this device does not have (including a repo.* id): the reference is resolved at runtime and simply not offered when it is missing, so a bundle is never broken by a dangling suggestion.

decades.description: rosary type only: { ordinalNoun | ordinalNounKey (the noun a decade is counted in — "Joy"/"Sorrow"/"Mystery"/"Decade"; the key form resolves in the praying language), announceMystery, entries: [{imageKey, isScripture? = true}] XOR count + fixedImageKey XOR source: "mysteryGroups" (the Rosary — decade catalog from the engine's mystery-group machinery: selection mode + liturgical calendar, group-labelled ordinals, single-mystery true ordinal, real Mystery values on steps), majorStep {title | titleKey, bodyKey, imageKey?}, minorStep {title | titleKey, bodyKey}, minorCount, preAnnouncement?: [Entry] (emitted BEFORE each decade's announcement, carrying the decade's subtitle but no decadeIndex — the Servite chaplet's invocation to Our Lady before each sorrow is named; postMinor could not express it, firing after a decade rather than before one), postMinor?: [Entry] (emitted after each decade's minors with the decade's subtitle/index — the Rosary's Glory Be/Fatima/eternal rest, gated with "if"), presenter?: {combinedTitle | combinedTitleKey, bodyKeys} (when the gating presenterMode option is on, the minors collapse into one combined step with hailMaryIndexInDecade = minorCount) }. Announcement steps pull title/body from the merged mystery tables by imageKey.

hours.description: hours type only: one entry per office of the day (Vespers, Compline, ...). Non-empty, ids unique.

propers.description: hours type only: every variable part of every office, each filed under the days it belongs to. This is the date→content resolution the type exists for — the engine picks, per slot, the matching proper of highest precedence (see DevotionProper.when).

closing.description: rosary and hours types: the rosary's closing sequence; for hours, prayed after every office (Compline's seasonal Marian antiphon is the motivating case, and the existing kind: "seasonalMarianAntiphon" entry serves it unchanged). days type has the same shared pair.

hasClosingCross.description: rosary type only; when true the closing cross must be the literal last step (bead-track invariant), and BeadLayout.build receives it.

DevotionHour.description: One office of an hours-type devotion — Vespers, Compline, the Office of Readings. Structurally a steps-type sequence: the parts that are the same every day are ordinary entries, the parts the calendar chooses are kind: "proper" slots. The bundle's shared opening/closing are prayed around it.

id.description: Unique within the bundle. Reserved purpose: which office a favorite opens on (a future Prayer.hourId, the way Prayer.dayIndex names a days-type day), and what a per-hour reminder is scheduled against.

name.description: English UI label (the app-wide convention); nameByLanguage overrides it per UI localization.

suggestedTime.description: "HH:mm" — the hour's traditional time, which a reminder for it should default to. Advisory exactly like a days-type series' suggestedReminderTime: the user's own reminder times always win. This is what makes the Angelus's reminderPresetHours generalize to an office of the day.

steps.description: Non-empty. Ordinary entries and kind: "proper" slots, in the order the office is prayed.

DevotionProper.description: One variable part of an office, filed under the days it belongs to — a page of the psalter, a proper of the season, a saint's collect. The engine resolves a slot by taking every proper whose "when" matches today and choosing the one of highest precedence.

when.description: The calendar facets this proper is constrained to, each a non-empty array of allowed values: date ("MM-DD", the sanctoral), rank (solemnity | feast | memorial | optionalMemorial | sunday | ferial — the vocabulary Shared/data/feasts.json already records, camelCased; a day with no entry is ferial), season (advent | christmas | lent | easterSeason | ordinary), week (>= 1, the week of the season), weekday (sun..sat), psalterWeek (1-4), readingYear (1 | 2, the Office of Readings' two-year cycle). Every declared facet must match (AND); within a facet any listed value matches (OR); an omitted facet is unconstrained. Absent or {} is the catch-all for its slot.

hour.description: Restricts this proper to one declared hour — Compline's psalmody does not follow Vespers'. Omitted = any hour that asks for the slot.

slot.description: The slot name this fills. Validator-enforced to be one some hour actually asks for, and (when hour is named) one that hour actually has.

steps.description: Non-empty; ordinary entries, resolved exactly like any other step's.

DevotionProper.precedence: Fixed facet order — date, rank, season, week, weekday, psalterWeek, readingYear — compared lexicographically: a proper constraining an earlier facet beats one that does not, regardless of how many facets either constrains. This is the Church's own hierarchy rather than a count of conditions (counting would let "Advent, week 3, Sunday" outrank Christmas Day, which is backwards). Ties go to the earlier declaration. The validator rejects two propers for one slot with an identical selector, so declaration order never silently decides an office.
DevotionProper.runtimeRequirement: The engine side of this type needs LiturgicalCalendarProviding to answer week-of-season, psalterWeek, rank and readingYear for a date — none of which it does today. psalterWeek is arithmetic on the week of the season, rank is a lookup in the feasts.json the Home screen already ships, and readingYear alternates with the liturgical year; only week-of-season is genuinely new computation. See ARCHITECTURE.md's "Hours".

DevotionAudioTrack.description: One narrated recording a bundle declares in its audio.json (a separate optional bundle file, staged by both packers like options.json) — loaders parse the metadata eagerly and serve the bytes on demand; each platform's player extracts them to a cache file and plays them on the prayer flow's transport bar (see ARCHITECTURE.md's "Audio"). Files are Ogg Opus (RFC 7845, .opus) under the bundle's audio/ directory.

id.description: Unique within the bundle — what a future playback position would persist against.

language.description: One of the manifest's languages; a recording is in one language.

file.description: Bundle-relative path; must live under audio/ and end in .opus (validator-enforced, plus the Ogg Opus signature of the file itself).

variantId.description: The steps-type variant this recording follows (traditional vs. scriptural Stations recordings differ). Must name a declared variant; null for single-form devotions.

name.description: English UI label (the app-wide convention); nameByLanguage overrides it per UI localization. Absent = platforms label the track by its language.

chapters.description: Non-empty; first chapter starts at 0, starts strictly increasing. Kept as JSON metadata rather than embedded Ogg chapter comments because none of the three platforms' media stacks surface those.

DevotionAudioChapter.description: One seek point of a DevotionAudioTrack.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the track.

title.description: Literal English display string. Mutually exclusive with titleKey (the step-entry convention).

titleKey.description: Content key resolved through the track language's ordinary content chain.

stepIndex.description: Advisory index into the built default-options step sequence — a hint for the future playback UI's step-syncing, never an invariant (the built sequence is option/calendar-dependent).

CustomDevotionOption.description: One user-configurable setting a bundle declares in its options.json (a separate bundle file, staged by both packers like catalog.json) — a toggle or a multi-case choice. Entry-level "if" expressions gate steps on the resulting values; the generic-devotion editor renders one schema-driven row per option. First real use: the Franciscan Crown's optional closing devotions (seventyTwoHailMarys, popeIntentions — both default true so the traditional sequence is unchanged).

key.description: Unique within the bundle; what entry "if" expressions and Prayer.customOptions key on.

name.description: English UI label (the app-wide convention); nameByLanguage overrides it per UI localization.

default.description: A JSON boolean for a toggle, a case id for a choice. Exposed to the engines/editor in canonical string form ("true"/"false" or the case id) — the same encoding Prayer.customOptions stores.

languages.$ref: See LanguageCatalog.all in ARCHITECTURE.md — la (default), en, ar (RTL), he (RTL), ru, tl

persistence.perDevotionDefaultScoping: save()/delete() clear or promote isDefault scoped to (Prayer.kind, Prayer.customDevotionId), never across devotions — two generic devotions must not steal each other's default slot. Legacy rows with retired per-devotion kinds resolve through the same identity (iOS PresetEntry.resolvedKind / Android PresetEntity.resolvedKind / Windows's SQL migration). See ARCHITECTURE.md#persistence.
